description:
Make nextest profile-fixture receipts bind to the Cargo target that produced the running setup and test artifacts, so reused binaries compiled in an isolated worktree cannot redirect consumers to that worktree's cache.

## Background

The full cargo-ci gate can reuse a `target/debug/jit` setup binary whose compile-time `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` names a temporary agent worktree while the current unit-test executable names the main checkout. The setup publishes its receipt under the temporary worktree's inferred `target`, but consumers independently infer the main checkout's `target` and reject the otherwise valid receipt as outside their cache. Cache-root identity must follow the actual Cargo artifact location or an equally exact runtime contract, not a source path embedded in a reused artifact.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Profiled-repository setup and consumers derive one canonical cache root from the actual Cargo target/artifact context, including default, absolute custom, and relative custom target-directory executions, without trusting an arbitrary receipt path.
- [hard] REQ-02: A deterministic regression uses setup and consumer executables whose compile-time checkout provenance differs while their runtime target is shared, and proves a valid same-run receipt succeeds instead of falling back or escaping the cache.
- [hard] REQ-03: Existing wrong-run, wrong-SHA, non-ordinary, corrupt, occupied, wrong-cache, scenario-provenance, isolated-clone, and atomic no-replace contracts remain fail-closed, with direct cargo-test fallback unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: The previously failing profiled re-init identity passes through the nextest setup path, focused fixture tests pass, formatting and warning-free linting pass, and the authoritative cargo-ci and code-review gates are green.

## Notes

Keep the fix inside test support. Do not weaken cache-root validation, trust a receipt-selected root, change production storage behavior, or edit nextest filters.
title: Bind profile fixture cache roots to runtime artifacts
